sentences.text: Yizhousaurus means "Yizhou lizard," honoring the Chuxiong Yi Autonomous Region where it was found. This animal holds the distinction of being the most complete basal sauropod dinosaur known to science that possesses an intact skull.

The holotype skeleton — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in 2002 and excavated between October 20 and November 23. Although the name was mentioned in a 2010 abstract, Yizhousaurus was not validly named and described until 2018.
Yizhousaurus is classified as a sauropod dinosaur within the Saurischia order.
Yizhousaurus lived during the Lower Jurassic period in the Lufeng Formation of Yunnan Province, southern China. It lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.
